summary: Sacred call (max 2 uses): every Red Button charm you have equipped needs 1 fewer charge to be ready again, permanently (never below 1).
tip: Pick it once your Red Button charms are on the table; charms bought later keep full cost. Ring Bell (3 to 2) and Midas Touch (4 to 3) then fire noticeably more often.

effects.text: Only Red Button charms equipped when you pick it get cheaper (minimum 1 charge); charms bought afterwards keep their normal charge cost.

synergies.why: Needs 2 charges instead of 3: +1 Symbols Multiplier every 2 Rounds instead of every 3.
Needs 3 charges instead of 4, so its permanent value Rounds come every 3 Rounds instead of 4.
Needs 4 charges instead of 5 (3 after a second pick), so its yellow retrigger Rounds come sooner.
At 1 charge it can flip every Round, gaining its Patterns Multiplier twice as fast.
The pick fires twice: 2 fewer charges on every equipped Red Button charm.
Discarding it later fires the call again for the Red Button charms you own by then.

assumptions: Assumed the cheaper cost stays with each charm even if it is moved to a drawer and back.
The engine applies the reduction to all Red Button charms, including ones bought later.

summary: Sacred call: gives every charm in the store a random Trait, then makes one of them free.
tip: Repeatable ticket saver: a free charm that also carries a Trait. Buy the cheap charms you want first so the free pick is likelier to land on a pricey one. Traits raise most other prices.

synergies.why: Every traited charm you equip adds +1 Patterns Multiplier.
Avid and Ambitious Traits rolled here become x2 multipliers.
Takes 1 ticket off the other charms, which the Traits made pricier.

assumptions: 'Modify' read as applying a random Trait (the wording later DLC cards use for Traits).
Assumed the free charm is chosen at random among the charms in the store.
Phone-applied random Traits are equally likely (wiki), so about 1 in 7 is Devious.

summary: Sacred call (once per run): every Pattern triggers one extra time for the rest of the run, doubling Pattern payouts.
tip: Take it on sight. Megaphone or Barathrum turn the single use into more permanent triggers, and the extra triggers also count for Pentacle, the Cats and other Pattern-count charms.

synergies.why: The one allowed pick fires twice: Patterns trigger 2 extra times for good.
Discarding it later adds a second permanent extra trigger.
Phone abilities trigger once more, so the pick gives +2 triggers.
Doubled Pattern counts make its 5+ Pattern growth spins far more common.
7+ Pattern spins become common, each paying double your Interest.
A doubled Jackpot spin is about 20 Patterns, past its 15+ trigger.

summary: Sacred call: spawns a random Sacred charm on your table (even past your slot limit), then halves the coins you are holding.
tip: Deposit or spend coins before answering to shrink the loss. Most Sacred charms trigger on 999s, so extra 666/999 odds (Devious Traits, Necronomicon) make them stronger.

synergies.why: Fires twice: two Sacred charms, though your coins are halved twice.
Discarding it later spawns another Sacred charm.
Phone abilities trigger once more: two Sacred charms per call.
In Sacred Mode its +3% 666 chance means more 999s for the Sacred charms.
The spawned Sacred charm arrives with a random Trait.

assumptions: Only coins in hand are halved, not deposited coins (per the wiki's strategy note).
Assumed effects that raise 666 odds raise 999 odds in Sacred Mode.

summary: Sacred call: doubles the current value of every small Pattern (3 or fewer Symbols: HOR, VER, DIAG and the 2-symbol ones).
tip: Best while small Patterns still pay most of your coins. It doubles current values, so take value adders first (I'm thinking of some strategies, Diesel Locomotive), then double.

synergies.why: Adds base value to the same small Patterns; take it first so the doubling includes it.
The 2-symbol Patterns it adds are small Patterns, so they are doubled too.
Grows every Pattern by its base value; doubling a grown value gains more.

summary: Sacred call: doubles the current value of every large Pattern (4+ Symbols: HOR-L, HOR-XL, ZIG, ZAG, ABOVE, BELOW, EYE, JACKPOT).
tip: Best in Luck and Jackpot builds, where big Patterns earn most of your coins. It doubles current values, so add first (I found a winning strategy) and stack it with I can't quit now.

synergies.why: Adds base value to the same large Patterns; take it first so the doubling includes it.
Doubles the Jackpot again: the two multiply.
Luck +7 on the last spin forms the big Patterns this doubles.
Forces Above or Below, both doubled by this call.
Forces Zig and Zag every 7 spins, both doubled by this call.
Its Above/Below doublings multiply with this one.

summary: The default Memory Card: no effects, a normal run.
tip: The neutral baseline. Use it to learn the game or when no other card fits your plan; every other card bends the rules for better or worse.

summary: Run-long: the store shows only 3 charms instead of 4, but every Deadline starts with 2 free Restocks.
tip: Free Restocks carry over: bank them for Shopping Cart (+2 Symbols Multiplier each) or spend them to grow Bell Pepper. Fewer store slots make Cigarettes rerolls worse.

effects.text: For the whole run the store has 3 charm slots instead of 4.

synergies.why: Each held free Restock is +2 Symbols Multiplier, and 2 more arrive every Deadline.
Each Restock spent this Deadline adds +2 to its Luck bonus.
Every Restock recharges a Red Button charm.
Doubles the free Restocks you are holding.

antiSynergies.why: With 3 slots its restock-and-reappear trick shows fewer new charms per buy.

assumptions: Free Restocks can be stockpiled between Deadlines (wiki strategy note).
